title: Jim Sarbh Shaved His Head for Real and Made a Show Without a Single Curse Word. India Might Send It to the Emmys.
excerpt: 'Made In India: A Titan Story' is the quiet word-of-mouth hit of the summer — a corporate drama about a wristwatch that families are watching together without skipping a frame. Now its producer says a second Emmy nomination for Sarbh is firmly on the table.
body:
There is a moment in every great underdog story where the people who made it realize they've made something bigger than they planned. For the team behind ***Made In India: A Titan Story***, that moment arrived as a piece of audience feedback so disarming it became the show's calling card: *"For so many years, we haven't sat together and watched something. This is the first show we watched without forwarding a single frame."*

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=MPNexsJZycw</youtube>

In an era of gore-soaked thrillers and gaali-laden crime sagas, the streaming hit of the summer is a six-episode period drama about a wristwatch. And it's quietly, deservedly, everywhere.

The series, which premiered on **Amazon MX Player** on June 3, chronicles the birth of **Titan** — the audacious 1980s bet that India could build a world-class consumer brand from a failing Tata Press. At its center is **Xerxes Desai**, the visionary who pivoted humiliation into history, played by the always-magnetic **Jim Sarbh**. Opposite him, **Naseeruddin Shah** plays the towering **JRD Tata** with the weathered gravity only Naseer can summon. Directed by **Robbie Grewal** and based on Vinay Kamath's book, it's been embraced not just by binge-watchers but by the business world — entrepreneurs and CEOs passing it around like a sacred text on Indian ambition.

And now there's Emmy talk, which is where this gets delicious.

Sarbh is no stranger to the room. He earned an International Emmy nomination for ***Rocket Boys***, and producer **Prabhleen Sandhu** has made it clear the team intends to chase a second.

> "For sure. Jim has outdone himself. He has got even the smallest nuances so right. So, we'll surely apply for it — why not?" — Prabhleen Sandhu, producer

The prep behind the performance is the kind of detail that wins awards conversations before the awards even open. Writer **Karan Vyas** revealed that Sarbh shaved his head for the role — *for real* — and that the show uses zero prosthetics. *"Usually actors wear wigs to go bald,"* Sandhu laughed. *"For Jim, it was vice versa."* It's the sort of total commitment that separates a good performance from a transformation, and on screen it shows: Sarbh disappears into Desai so completely that viewers who lived through Titan's rise have called the resemblance uncanny.

What makes ***Made In India*** quietly radical is what it refuses to do. No item songs. No gangsters. No bloodshed. The only villain, Sandhu notes, is a smuggler with a gun and very limited screen time. Audiences have started calling it a *"detox"* — a show you can watch with your parents, your kids, and your grandparents in the same room, which in 2026 is practically a genre unto itself. For a diaspora audience raised on the idea that prestige drama must be punishing to be good, it's a gentle, persuasive rebuttal.

There's a poignant note threading through the production too. Vyas, reflecting on the show's reception, sighed that he wished **Ratan Tata** — who died in 2024 — had lived to see it. *"He would have been VERY happy,"* he said. The series lands as a tribute not just to one watch brand but to an entire generation of Indian builders who decided the country didn't have to import its self-respect.

For NRIs, the where-to-watch is the easy part and the catch in the same breath. ***Made In India: A Titan Story*** streams on **Amazon MX Player**, available in Hindi, Tamil and Telugu — but MX Player's footprint outside India is thin, so diaspora viewers will want to check regional availability or lean on a family member's Indian login. Given the show's word-of-mouth momentum, a wider international window feels less like a hope than an inevitability.

Sandhu has also confirmed the title was chosen with sequels in mind. ***Made In India*** isn't meant to be one watch brand's story — it's a banner, an anthology of Indian origin stories waiting to be told. *"It may not always be about a brand,"* she said. *"It can also be about a person. But it has to suit the 'Made In India' idea."*

Which means the smartest thing about this sleeper hit may be its name. One show became a hit. The franchise it implies — a gallery of the dreamers who built modern India, one episode at a time — could become something the diaspora has been waiting decades to see: its own ambition, finally rendered as prestige television, and possibly, with a bald and brilliant Jim Sarbh leading the charge, with an Emmy on the mantel to prove it.
